text: How to play onchain if BTC continues to trend up BTC is approaching 80k and its first major resistance to starting a new uptrend. Onchain looks completely different to 12-18 months ago, but the fundamentals of playing a trending market haven't changed much. It's why 2nd/3rd/4th cyclers can keep up with the new gen without matching their screen time, they already know how flows behave when risk appetite expands. 1. Established tokens/eco's During the downtrend it was still anyone's game because rotations were aggressive. If BTC keeps trending up, I think we already have most of the information needed to know where the leading eco's/assets will be. Sol remains the home of attention and breeding ground for fast moving experiments. The infra from devs to traders can support almost any narrative, product or execution with very little friction. RH is the clear #2 imo, with a genuine chance to rival Sol if it builds comparable infra for traders/devs while finding creative ways to attract new flows. Until proven otherwise, drifting too far outside these two probably does more harm than good. There isn't enough excess capital yet to support several chains like you see deeper into a bull. New eco's will still offer asymmetric opportunities, but dethroning Sol/RH after they built foundational strength through the bear is a harder trade. Flagship memes/tokens should continue acting as strong betas (Ansem, Cashcat, Pump etc). Mid caps also get a real chance to break price ceilings if leaders push into the billions. We haven't had a new pair hit escape velocity in a long time. I think that changes soon. 2. New pairs Every strong onchain run tends to start with a mid 8 fig/low 9 fig runner over 48ish hours. The faster and further it goes, the better the signal for appetite over the following weeks. Narrative quality is crucial. Penguin was a viral TikTok meme with what looked like heavy MM'ing from Pump. Ansem is a longer lasting blended utility meme that can't easily be replicated and has multiple potential attention waves/catalysts. We've already seen 8 fig runners almost daily this past month. As the mini manias continue, bundling/crime will become more sophisticated. The gems are coins that are difficult to vamp and have unique merit (utility, public backing from a head figure, substantial lore, first mover advantage etc). Novel experiments from credible devs are also far more likely to succeed on leading chains unless a new narrative centric chain emerges. Memes are similar, although hunting upcoming eco's for first movers/crime remains a high RR use of time because the new pair meme game itself is now so efficient. 3. Old coins/utility tokens Old coins are much more selective. In previous metas you normally had a handful of teams that weren't vaporware and were still building products with real users. Real products take months/years, so by the time the narrative returns the token has often already drawn down >90%. Two ways this usually plays out: 1. Longer term innovation trends (private inference, robotics, DeSci, stablecoins etc). When attention rotates back, I want the pure play with the architecture/economics that makes the most sense to scale. 2. News catalysts. Claude gets banned by the U.S. government -> private inference sends. Elon announces a Neuralink breakthrough -> DeSci sends. The most important part of these trades is optics: what looks like the cleanest, most credible and most obvious vehicle for the market to express the narrative through. Ironically, these are often the trades that feel too easy because they're staring you in the face. They're generally short lived and I'm looking to exit inside a 1-7 day window. Missing plenty here and this could easily be a full article, but this is the TLDR of how I'd separate the main onchain metas if BTC keeps trending.
